This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #14882: Very similar request — both identify the same root cause (absolutist language in `plan.txt`/plan mode system prompt) and propose softening restrictions to allow certain operations while keeping source code protected. That issue also references the same files (`prompt/plan.txt`, `prompt.ts`) and proposes making the read-only constraint configurable or context-aware.

**Patch revised** — fixed a second issue: when `part.metadata` is `undefined`, the previous version set `providerMetadata: undefined` explicitly. The AI SDK treats a present-but-undefined key differently from an absent key, causing Anthropic to still reject the block. Updated to a conditional spread so the key is only included when the value exists.

Note: this fix operates at the session reconstruction layer. There are complementary bugs at the provider transform layer — #23755 addresses three cases where thinking blocks get dropped or modified before even reaching this layer. Without those fixes, this one alone may not be sufficient in all scenarios. Related prior attempts: #16750, #21370.

I had the same issue and met the requirements (Java version 21 or higher). When I enabled debug logging, I noticed that the server wasn't detecting the correct Java version. After checking the code, I found this line:
[https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/9b6db08d2144c33ec34cd88026774f847ec79761/packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts#L1102](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/9b6db08d2144c33ec34cd88026774f847ec79761/packages/opencode/src/lsp/server.ts#L1102)

It seems the LSP expects the Java version to have three digits, but my installed Java only displayed one, e.g. `openjdk "21" ...`. I updated to the latest version, which now reports three digits `openjdk "21.0.10" 2026-01-20 LTS`, and after that the LSP started working correctly in OpenCode.

Hey @HendrikPetertje, thanks for digging into this and sharing the patch!

So regarding the two things you found:

MCP tools not loading: I haven't been able to reproduce this on my end. I tested with kiro-cli 2.0.1 and opencode's MCP tools (both built-in ones like read/write/bash and external MCP servers configured in opencode.json) work correctly.

Regarding the kiro agent: To give you a little bit more detail, the way the Kiro provider works is that it sets up an IPC adapter and an MCP bridge in between opencode and kiro-cli. The objective of this is to allow the provider to leverage opencode's built in tools and ecosystem of plugins and agents and effectively use Kiro ACP to act as an LLM. The custom agent that you see in .kiro/agents is a kiro custom agent that registers the MCP bridge as its tools, so that it can only "see" and call the tools that opencode exposes. when you configure an MCP in opencode.json and you initiate a conversation, the provider will see it as another more tool and register it in the MCP bridge, allowing Kiro ACP to call it.
The reason to have an agent per opencode directory is to allow them to register different set of tools (so that you can run several instances of it in parallel), if we were to store it in the global config that'd probably collide.

The approach in your patch adds the MCP servers directly to kiro-cli alongside the bridge, which effectively bypasses it for those tools and has Kiro ACP directly executing them. I decided to have all tools register in the MCP Bridge so that we ensure that it is opencode the one that executes them.

Did you have the MCP server issues before or after updating kiro-cli? I just tested it with version 2.0.1
